strings.name: Carl Lewis
strings.role: Sprint and long-jump champion · Athletics coach
strings.summary: Lewis won nine Olympic gold medals across sprints, long jump and relays, including four consecutive Olympic long-jump titles. His combination of speed and jumping technique helped define international athletics in the 1980s and 1990s. He later coached at Houston. Low-level stimulant findings from 1988 became controversial in 2003; the IAAF upheld the original clearance after review.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A multiple Olympic sprint and long-jump champion who shaped international competitive standards in modern athletics.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Nine Olympic golds
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won gold at four Olympics from 1984 to 1996, including four successive long-jump titles.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Entered the University of Houston in 1979 and trained under Tom Tellez.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Speed and jumping
strings.highlights.h2.text: Combined world-class sprint championships with sustained long-jump success.
strings.timeline.t1.title: University head coach
strings.timeline.t1.text: Appointed Houston track-and-field head coach after serving as an assistant.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Review of historic tests
strings.timeline.t2.text: Low-level stimulant positives from 1988 became public; the IAAF upheld the original inadvertent-use clearance.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Fourth Olympic long-jump title
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won in Atlanta, taking his ninth Olympic gold medal.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Two Barcelona golds
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won the long jump and men's 4×100m relay.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Tokyo World Championships
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the 100m in a then-world-record 9.86; finished behind Mike Powell in long jump.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Seoul Olympics
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won long-jump gold and was confirmed 100m champion after Ben Johnson's disqualification.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Four Los Angeles golds
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won the 100m, 200m, long jump and 4×100m relay.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Three inaugural world titles
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the 100m, long jump and 4×100m relay in Helsinki.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Entered Houston
strings.timeline.t9.text: Developed sprint and long-jump technique under Tellez.
